plan.summary: This 1-4 block is a simple off-camp strength and power build for boxing with one short session per week and bodyweight-only equipment. Week 1 establishes a safe baseline with a push-up strength assessment so future progress is easier to track, and the main training starts in Week 2. The sessions stay full-body, power first, then main strength, then trunk and neck work in brief doses so they support boxing practice without adding unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general full-body strength, jumping ability, trunk stiffness, and basic speed without chasing fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress bodyweight strength and explosive intent with slightly harder variations while keeping sessions short and clean.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength you built and express it with faster, sharper, boxing-friendly power and speed work.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can with a quiet landing. Reset between reps and stop if height drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the countermovement makes timing messy. Start from a still quarter squat and drive up fast.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if jump landings are not yet confident. Keep contacts light and springy.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use this session to establish your baseline. Warm up with a few easy sets, then do one hardest clean set in the 3-10 rep range, stopping only when form would break on the next rep.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then perform one hardest clean set of 3-10 reps. Log the reps so the app can use this as your starting strength reference for future progress.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean set and keep every rep strict from chest to full lockout.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor push-ups are too hard to keep strict. Elevate the hands enough to stay in the target rep range with clean reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Knee Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if needed to stay pain-free and controlled. Keep a straight line from knees to shoulders.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a controlled lower and drive up hard. Keep the front foot flat and torso tall.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squat balance is awkward. Step back under control and push through the front leg.

substitutionOptions.name: Bodyweight Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if knees do not like split stance work. Stay smooth and own the bottom.

exercises.name: Prone Y-T-W Raise
exercises.notes: Move slowly and keep the shoulders down. This is for control, not fatigue.

substitutionOptions.name: Scapular Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor raises are uncomfortable. Keep elbows straight and move only through the shoulder blades.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Keep ribs down, hips high, and body straight from head to heel.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if side planks are too shaky. Brace hard and do not let the low back sag.

exercises.name: Supine Neck Isometric
exercises.notes: Use gentle hand resistance for flexion, extension, and each side. Keep effort smooth and stop if you feel pain or dizziness.

substitutionOptions.name: Wall Neck Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use the wall for light pressure if hand setup feels awkward. Keep the effort low and controlled.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump fast and land quietly. Take enough rest to keep every rep crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you move better from a paused start. Explode straight up.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this lower-impact option if jump landings are still inconsistent.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave 1-2 reps in reserve on every set. Keep the body straight and each rep identical.

performanceTarget.prompt: Build your best strict set inside the rep range while keeping one good rep in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Raise the hands if needed to keep the full rep range with clean form.

substitutionOptions.name: Knee Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor reps break down early. Keep tempo smooth and chest proud.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Control the way down and stand up with intent. Keep balance simple and steady.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: A good swap if split squats feel cramped. Step back softly and push tall.

substitutionOptions.name: Bodyweight Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if single-leg balance is the main limiter.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
exercises.notes: Move slowly with knees just off the floor. Keep hips level and shoulders active.

substitutionOptions.name: High Plank Shoulder Tap
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space is limited. Stay square and avoid rocking.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Press the low back into the floor and keep the ribs tucked. Shorten the lever if needed.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this easier option if you cannot hold position without arching.

exercises.name: Supine Neck Isometric
exercises.notes: Use light hand pressure only. Smooth effort, no jerking, and stop if anything feels off.

substitutionOptions.name: Wall Neck Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use the wall if that setup feels more stable and easier to control.

exercises.name: Squat Jump
exercises.notes: Pause briefly in a quarter squat, then explode up. Land softly and reset fully between reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the paused start makes you lose rhythm.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if impact tolerance is low that week.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Stay one rep shy of technical breakdown. If all sets are easy, use a slower lower for control.

performanceTarget.prompt: Match or beat last week with stricter reps or one extra rep while keeping form clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you cannot keep the full range strict across all sets.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a 3-second lower if normal push-ups are too easy in the rep range.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Step back under control and drive up through the front leg. Stay tall and do not rush the reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you prefer a fixed stance and more balance.

substitutionOptions.name: Bodyweight Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if stepping back bothers the knees.

exercises.name: Prone Swimmer
exercises.notes: Move slowly and keep tension around the upper back. Do not shrug toward the ears.

substitutionOptions.name: Prone Y-T-W Raise
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if swimmers feel too awkward to coordinate.

exercises.name: Side Plank With Reach
exercises.notes: Reach under with control, then open back up without losing hip height.

substitutionOptions.name: Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use the standard hold if the reach causes you to rotate too much.

exercises.name: Supine Neck Isometric
exercises.notes: Keep resistance light to moderate and breathing calm. Quality matters more than strain.

substitutionOptions.name: Wall Neck Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a steadier setup.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Keep the jumps fast and fresh. Stop while they still feel springy.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you feel better from a paused start.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this lower-impact option if legs feel heavy from boxing.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Deload week. Keep the reps clean, smooth, and well short of failure.

performanceTarget.prompt: Use this week to move cleanly and finish fresh rather than chase extra reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need an easier deload option.

substitutionOptions.name: Knee Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if shoulders feel beaten up and you want a lighter week.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Own the positions and keep every rep easy to repeat. This week is for fatigue relief.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it feels smoother on your hips.

substitutionOptions.name: Bodyweight Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this simplest option if you are unusually sore or tired.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
exercises.notes: Stay controlled and quiet. Do not turn this into conditioning.

substitutionOptions.name: High Plank Shoulder Tap
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space is tight or wrists need a simpler option.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Keep the shape crisp and stop before the low back lifts.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need an easier trunk option for the deload week.

exercises.name: Supine Neck Isometric
exercises.notes: Keep this very easy and smooth this week. Skip it if your neck feels irritated from sparring or bag work.

substitutionOptions.name: Wall Neck Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use the easiest setup that lets you stay relaxed and controlled.
